recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit as-is. Revisit only if Patient Care later decides that chat/messaging should be added as a Communication scope use case rather than handled through Communication.medium.
issue_request: Applied Patient Care issue resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. The reporter asked to add instant messaging / chat exchanges between patients and providers to the Communication use-case list; the final decision was that the scope bullets describe what was communicated rather than how, and that messaging/chat is represented through Communication.medium. The requested source change was to define Communication.medium as "A channel that was used for this communication (e.g. email, fax, SMS)."
initial_application: The Jira comment points to GH#d54806d. Commit d54806d151d3eccc0c6a5ec0d11ed0657a57890f, titled "J#25214 Add SMS to Communication.medium definition", added a J#25214 committee note to Communication.medium and changed the definition from "A channel that was used for this communication (e.g. email, fax)." to "A channel that was used for this communication (e.g. email, fax, SMS)."
additional_context: Communication is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/communication/structuredefinition-Communication.xml is in current build scope. The current Communication.medium element contains the J#25214 committee note, the SMS-inclusive definition, and the v3 ParticipationMode binding. Searches of Zulip and Confluence found no directly relevant conflicting community discussion; Confluence refs only surfaced agenda/minutes mentions without substantive resolution text.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current Communication StructureDefinition already contains the exact applied FHIR-25214 wording.
